newsitem.title: KENYA: FOCUS-Kenya shilling hits new official low.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Kenya shilling hits new official low.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling slid to a new official low against the dollar on Monday as foreign investors pulled out of the market because of continuing economic and political uncertainty, foreign exchange dealers said.
The shilling depreciated by 1.3 percent on Monday morning to trade at a commercial mean rate of 70.68 from 69.75 at the open.
The latest movements brought the shilling's total losses to 18.79 percent since the International Monetary Fund cancelled a key aid package to Kenya on July 31, citing corruption.
Dealers said the violence which flared in Mombasa, the country's second biggest city, last week was a blow to Kenya's international image and exposed the fragile currency to further vulnerability.
"It's chaotic right now. We were already at the bottom and now it looks like we're going to begin the slide again," a senior dealer told Reuters.
"It's going to affect the way they (investors) leave the market. Right now it looks like they just want to get out," a dealer said.
Some foreign investors pulled out on Monday despite an appeal last Friday by Central Bank of Kenya Governor Micah Cheserem for them to stay in East Africa's largest economy.

Cheserem, alarmed by a rapid outflow of dollars fuelled by the row with the IMF, made his appeal after investors pulled out of Thursday's weekly auction of high-yield treasury bills citing market uncertainty.
The bank only sold 50 percent of the 14 billion shillings of bills offered while about five billion shillings of treasury bills were not rolled over.
Cheserem has not intervened decisively to boost the shilling, saying he would allow the currency to fend for itself, but analysts say they feared he was deliberately allowing the shilling to weaken.
"It's not clear whether he wants the shilling to slide in favour of tourism and exporters. Maybe he has done this intentionally, not just because of the IMF," said a leading broker.
The IMF's suspension of the $205-million Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility (ESAF), over graft and poor governance, led the World Bank to delay its own disbursements of up to $71.6 million.

Tourism is Kenya's biggest source of jobs and hard currency, earning $465 million in 1996. Tour operators said they had received anxious calls from tour operators in Europe fearing for their clients safety amid media reports of violence.
"The image of Kenya is dented, cancellations will be there because people are worried," said Najib Balala, chairman of Mombasa and Coast Tourist Association.
More than 30 people have been killed since raiders struck villages, police posts and a tourist lodge in coastal areas south of Mombasa last Wednesday.

Police have blamed the attacks on thugs, but pamphlets distributed in the area have cited ethnic slogans for seizing regional power in general elections due later this year. No date for the poll has yet been set.
